text:
Carolina's 4-1 win in Philadelphia was a fair reflection of how the game was played, and it was settled in a single stretch of the second period. Andrei Svechnikov snapped one home at 10:16, Shayne Gostisbehere made it 2-0 at 13:45, and after Christian Dvorak tipped in a goal for PHI at 15:26 to cut it to 2-1, Sebastian Aho restored the two-goal lead at 16:54. Those three Carolina goals came in a span of about seven minutes, and the Flyers never got closer than one.

The numbers say CAR earned it. Carolina led in expected goals 3.23 to 1.57 and in shot attempts 59 to 41, and simulated replays of every shot give the Hurricanes a 79 percent chance to win, against 21 for PHI. CAR pressed from the opening period, out-chancing the Flyers 1.04 to 0.33 in expected goals before the scoring started. Neither team scored on the power play, with CAR 0 for 4 and PHI 0 for 3, so the game was decided at even strength.

In goal, Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 18 of 19 shots and finished 0.57 goals saved above expected, while Joseph Woll made 26 saves on 30 shots and came out 0.77 below expected. Mark Jankowski added the fourth goal at 15:09 of the third, the most likely scoring chance of the five goals at 22 percent. Taylor Hall had a 30 percent look in that period that Woll stopped. Svechnikov and Aho were named the first two stars, each with a goal and an assist, while Dvorak, who scored PHI's only goal, took the third. The result comes a week after CAR won 3-2 in overtime in the earlier meeting this season.
